chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: Quitting Meroff after a flare-up in Columbus
summary: Fed up and homesick at Mitchell, South Dakota, he gives notice after a quarrel in Columbus over a date, returning to Chicago in the Depression.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah and we were responsible for our own clothing; we had to keep those clean because they were furnished to us; we didn't buy them. That was Meroff's part of it--- well, anyway, when I got to -- the Corn Palace - was in Mitchell, South Dakota -- and, uh, I was really getting fed up with the whole business of travelling like that--- and I got kind of homesick to go back to Chicago and I know that a couple of the other fellows did too. And, I handed my notice in down there -- we had--- Meroff and I had had a little ---
Well, did that happen out in South Dakota---
I was-- oh, okay - go ahead.
You had a little flare up with Benny---

I had a flare up with Benny in Columbus, Ohio and I thought he was very unreasonable about not telling someone--- I had told him the day before that I had a date and would it be all right if I kept it for the following day -- he said, yes. And, then, he changed his mind and called a rehearsal -- and I went to the date anyway.

And, that really erked him to no end and we were both very sorry that we flared up because I had a great amount of respect for him - one of the finest band leaders I ever worked for and generous, as well. So, uh, I got--- I was hot-headed too as a kid and I quit and I went back to Chicago. And, so, that ended Meroff - Meroff had his wife, Florence---
Yes - that's right - that's right. And, she--- he didn't have the nerve to call me himself but she called and asked if I would come back and I had had it - really - I was really hurt about that---
Well, you had been with him for over five years---

Yeah - five years and I made a lot of money with him. But, what I didn't realize what I was getting into at this point is it took a lot of nerve to quit in 1931; we were in the middle of the Depression and I had never felt the depression at all---
